name: Vection
description: Vection demo: an endless banking flight down a city canyon at dusk, designed to make you feel self-motion from vision alone (motion warning: look away or lower intensity if you are prone to motion sickness). Research-informed: wide-field optic flow from dense high-contrast lit-window grids, lamps and lane dashes streaming out of a focus of expansion at the horizon; roll vection from a slow 0.055 / 0.13 Hz roll swing on top of the coordinated bank; slow 26 s / 71 s speed cycles (smooth acceleration); ride jitter and a beat-locked footstep bob; Fraser-Wilcox / Kitaoka peripheral-drift sawtooth friezes on curbs, shop fronts and rooflines; and a breakdown freeze that stops the flight when the music drops (motion aftereffect). Analytic ray-traced street (block DDA, two building rows, cross streets, wet mirror puddles, lamps, parallax motes, dusk sky), flight state integrated in a 5x1 rgba32f Feedback, rgba16f HDR render target, radial speed-blur lens with edge chromatic aberration, two-level bloom and anamorphic streak. Music: kick speed surges, beat bob and lamp swell, a lean on every bar, bass-breathing windows; identical when silent. Parameters panel: intensity, speed, roll, drift illusion, palette, fog, exposure, blur, aberration, bloom, music reactivity, breakdown freeze.

data.text:
# Vection
An endless banking flight down a city canyon at dusk, tuned to make your body feel the motion: a sense of self-motion (vection) from vision alone. Look at the centre and let the edges stream.
Motion warning: this patch is designed to produce a sensation of moving, tilting and falling. If you are prone to motion sickness, look away or lower intensity if it gets uncomfortable.
Reacts to music: open the audio menu → Mic (speed surges on the kick, footstep bob on the beat, a lean on every bar, and the flight freezes at breakdowns).
## The science
- Wide-field optic flow: dense lit windows, lamps and lane dashes stream out of a focus of expansion at the horizon, densest in the periphery.
- Roll vection: the whole view rolls slowly (0.055 + 0.13 Hz) on top of the bank of the curves, so the floor seems to tilt.
- Speed changes slowly (26 s and 71 s cycles): smooth acceleration drives linear vection harder than a constant speed.
- Jitter and bob: a small ride shake and a beat-locked footstep bob make the motion feel bodily.
- Peripheral drift (Fraser-Wilcox / Kitaoka): sawtooth friezes on curbs, shop fronts and rooflines seem to stream toward you even when nothing moves.
- Motion aftereffect: when the music drops the flight eases to a stop, and the frozen city seems to drift backwards.
## Tweak it in the Parameters panel
Press P (or the sliders button in the top bar): Flight, Look, Lens and Music settings with pretty names; hover a name for what it does, double-click a slider to reset it.
Double-click a group box to open it, Esc to come back.

## Motion (vection controller)
A 5x1 rgba32f Feedback holds the flight state; Vection Motion integrates it every frame, so speed changes stay smooth and continuous.
- Linear vection: speed follows slow 26 s / 71 s acceleration cycles; on the kick it surges forward (held, eased).
- Roll vection: roll = bank of the curve + a slow swing (0.055 and 0.13 Hz, ±roll × intensity) + a lean that eases in on each bar.
- Jitter: a 3-7 Hz ride shake that grows with speed; on the beat a footstep bob and nod.
- Breakdown: a fast and a slow level follower; when the level falls far below its recent average while music was playing, the flight eases to a stop (motion aftereffect), then surges back on the drop.
- It also stores the focus of expansion for the lens.

## City Canyon (optic flow)
Vection City ray-traces the street analytically (no raymarching): two rows of buildings per side (block DDA, setbacks, cross streets), a wet street with mirror puddles, lamps every 24 m, motes on 10 depth planes and a dusk sky.
- Periphery: high-contrast window grids, lamps and lane dashes give dense flow at the edges, where vection is driven.
- Ground plane + horizon: the street and the sun at the end of the canyon pin the focus of expansion and make the roll read as a tilting floor.
- Parallax: near facades, the back row, motes and clouds move at different rates.
- Peripheral drift: curbs, shop-front friezes and rooflines carry a luminance sawtooth (black → dark gray → white → light gray toward you), which seems to stream toward you.
Patterns fade to their mean before they can alias, so nothing flickers.

## Render Targets
The HDR frame (rgba16f, alpha = nearness) feeds the lens. A downsampled bright pass and a smaller blur level feed the bloom.

## Bloom
Two blurred bright-pass levels and a horizontal anamorphic streak, added back as light.

## Lens & Post
Vection Lens streaks the frame radially away from the focus of expansion. The streak is longer at speed, for near surfaces and toward the edges (speed lines), with chromatic aberration growing toward the edges. Then bloom, ACES, saturation, a light vignette (the periphery must stay bright) and grain.

## Music
The audio level gates everything: with the audio off or silent, drive = 0 and the flight looks exactly the same. drive = music × smoothstep(0.02, 0.12, level).
- Kick: the speed surges forward (inside Vection Motion, u_kick × drive).
- Beat: a footstep bob and nod of the camera; lamps and motes swell (BeatEnvelope ad × drive) as a soft brightness swell, not a strobe.
- Bar: the roll leans to a new angle, easing in over the first 60% of each bar.
- Bass: lit windows breathe (up to +15%).
- Breakdown: the flight eases to a stop when the level drops well below its recent average (Parameters panel → Breakdown freeze).
Beat-phase couplings (bob, nod, bar lean, lamp pulse) are also scaled by the beat tracker's confidence (u_beatConfidence), so they fade in as the beat locks and out when it is lost, and run on the stable beat clock with its certainty gate (BeatEnvelope gate: fade; x smoothstep(0.25, 0.75, u_beatTrust) in Vection Motion): after a track change the clock holds the old tempo, then glides to the new one without jumps, and these couplings fade out until the new beat is trusted. Level and band couplings (kick surge, bass) are not.

data.label: Intensity
data.description: Roll, speed swings, jitter, peripheral illusion and blur together. Lower it if the motion gets uncomfortable.

data.label: Drift illusion
data.description: Contrast of the peripheral-drift sawtooth friezes (Fraser-Wilcox / Kitaoka).

data.label: Palette
data.description: 0 ember dusk, 1 blue hour, 2 neon night (in-between values blend).

data.label: Music reactivity
data.description: 0 = ignore the music. Speed surges on the kick, footstep bob on the beat, a lean on every bar.

data.label: Breakdown freeze
data.description: 1 = the flight eases to a stop when the music drops (motion aftereffect); 0 = keep flying.
